speakers.name: Ilya Yuffa
speakers.title: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities

exchanges.question: Investors focus on incretin pricing more than volume; at a high level, what are Lilly's margins under a wide range of price scenarios, and how do manufacturing investments add to the competitive moat?
exchanges.answer: Five or six quarters into a post-shortage world, Lilly can pursue volume expansion aggressively; with out-of-pocket pay (75% of ex-US Mounjaro business, a meaningful portion in the US) volume expansion is quite expansionary, perhaps non-linear, to price cuts, though there is a floor. Q1 price effects were mainly negotiated outcomes with governments (MFN package, China diabetes access). Unit economics are driven by fixed costs sunk or unmovable, and Lilly has margin latitude but will invest in future medicines. No margin figures were given.

exchanges.question: What are the learnings from the better-than-expected international Mounjaro launch, and should generic semaglutide in select markets affect the ramp?
exchanges.answer: Mounjaro is fully launched in more than 55 countries with rapid share gains, with estimated share of 60% in Brazil and Korea (launched 2H 2025) plus China type 2 NRDL reimbursement. Early India data (a few weeks) suggest generics stimulate market growth; Mounjaro prescriptions are about 10% higher in recent weeks than before generics entered. Share is above 53% (average) and incremental gains are getting harder; expect very strong continued year-on-year growth and some sequential growth, with Europe holiday seasonality in H2.

exchanges.question: How is the obesity market segmenting, and where will retatrutide, Foundayo and eloralintide each open up the market?
exchanges.answer: Patients worldwide number perhaps in the billions and will want medicines tailored to needs; early innings with single agonists, dual agonists and now orals. Retatrutide suits those seeking greater weight loss but also elsewhere across the spectrum; eloralintide suits patients wanting a non-GLP-1 mechanism or as add-on to incretins. Other ideas include less frequent dosing and ultra long-acting genetic medicines; the final market split is hard to prognosticate and many ideas share manufacturing platforms.

exchanges.question: What is the strategy to activate Medicare patients, when does it play out (Q4 2026 or 2027), and how does the attractive price point affect persistence?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Part D access for obesity starts in July and runs through 2027; millions of Part D beneficiaries have obesity. Physician, pharmacy and consumer education will take time, so 2026 will be a gradual path with continued growth in 2027. Zepbound and Mounjaro already have great persistency relative to other chronic conditions, and the $50 a month copay will add to that.

exchanges.question: What do immunology, neuroscience and oncology need to match the scale of the obesity and metabolic business, and is it BD or something else?
exchanges.answer: Those businesses are growing extremely fast; without obesity and metabolic, Lilly would be surely one of the fastest-growing pharma companies. Each area has significant unmet need to scale into, and BD is part of the answer, citing Centessa (sleep-wake medicines) and Orna (immune reset).

exchanges.question: With a few weeks of Foundayo launch and about 15,000 patients started, how confident is Lilly in the launch curve framing (below oral Wegovy initially, accelerating in H2)? How much Foundayo contribution is in the guidance range?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa: early days but encouraging; over 8,000 prescribers, a third of whom had not written an oral GLP-1; commercial access confirmed at two of the large PBMs by mid-May and Medicare access starts early July; just over 20,000 patients treated to date, 80% new to class; full DTC and TV in Q3. Montarce: the guide increase is driven by the entire portfolio; Foundayo is tracking to expectations after three weeks of data, but no Foundayo contribution figure was given.

exchanges.question: With Bridge extending into 2027, what is next, and is Lilly working on longer-term Medicare access?
exchanges.answer: The agreement with the administration had a 2027 commitment as a contingency if Part D plans did not opt in at a certain rate, and they did not. Bridge access at $50 a month should drive persistency, and over an 18-month window population-level health improvements may appear. He expects the government to push for Part D participation in 2028, with more news as 2026 ends.

exchanges.question: What are the steps and mechanics to convince employers to buy into the Employer Connect program?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Commercial access has been steady around 50%. Employer Connect works with third parties to speak to employers, with a transparent known price and flexible employer-employee contribution design. The 2026 selling cycle has passed, so impact will most likely be gradual in H2 2026 with incremental opt-ins for 2027.

exchanges.question: How is Lilly thinking about leveraging its scale in the DTC channel and its portfolio on the commercial side?
exchanges.answer: Ricks: consumer digital platforms are here to stay and a big part of the business; expect continuous improvement in the US experience and national expansion, and a platform for more preventative medicines. Yuffa: around 55% of Zepbound new patient starts are self-pay, mostly through LillyDirect or telehealth, and about 45% of early Foundayo volume comes through LillyDirect. Jonsson: outside the US patient activation will drive most growth, with a slower ramp.

exchanges.question: Q1 Zepbound US implies about $580 per prescription (about $550 adjusted) versus roughly $450 cash price; what explains the delta?
exchanges.answer: Montarce: the math is spot on; excluding the November MFN agreement, prices have been relatively stable quarter on quarter, LillyDirect prices were lowered from December and are stable, and the remainder is the commercial business. Ricks: a reasonable amount of medical exception and OSA usage moves across channels at close to an undiscounted price.

exchanges.question: How does the Foundayo launch compare to a traditional primary care launch, what is being accelerated or held back, given the inventory prepared?
exchanges.responderTitle: President, Lilly USA and Global Customer Capabilities
exchanges.answer: Yuffa: same three elements as primary care launches (prescriber base, access, consumer awareness), with access gained earlier (two of three PBMs in a couple of weeks, Part D in July); DTC digital and social was activated in week one but full DTC is being held until physicians understand the profile. Ricks: the products are line extensions so Foundayo starts from lower brand and molecule awareness; inventory speaks to the international rollouts, with 40 countries under review and launches as 2026 ends into next year.

exchanges.question: What is the vision for US employer coverage, versus coverage with greater cost-sharing for consumers using LillyDirect?
exchanges.answer: Obesity medicines should be broadly covered and the July 1 Medicare start sets a standard with spillover into commercial. The path will not be a straight line and obesity is the last thing in because it is a broad disease (70% of adults have overweight or obesity), easier to say no to. Employer Connect creates new options to get to yes, new indications will help, and progress will be incremental quarter on quarter.
